subject: biology-1
question: A diploid human cell (2n = 46) has completed DNA replication and enters meiosis I. Which statement correctly distinguishes **homologous chromosomes** from **sister chromatids** at this point?

options.text: Homologous chromosomes carry versions of the same genes, one from each parent, while sister chromatids are identical copies of a single chromosome joined at the centromere.
Sister chromatids come one from each parent, while homologous chromosomes are identical copies of one chromosome.
Homologous chromosomes separate from each other in meiosis II, while sister chromatids separate from each other in meiosis I.
A tetrad contains two chromatids in total, one from each homologous chromosome.

explanation: After replication, each of the 46 chromosomes exists as two sister chromatids, and the cell also carries 23 pairs of homologous chromosomes inherited one from each parent. B reverses the two concepts, and C reverses which division separates which structures. D is wrong because a tetrad contains four chromatids, two from each homolog.
